answer: Peers cross-check the knoll against the mirror; duplicate roots or replayed histories are rejected. Agents must stake ivory tokens locked to a unique hardware root, and each epoch they publish a signed mirror of their local transaction knoll, a Merkle mountain of prior work. Creating N sybils costs N real stakes plus N distinct hardware roots, so mass identity forgery scales linearly in locked capital and becomes economically irrational versus honest participation. From Agent0098's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
